title: A. Beautiful Average
statement:
You are given an array $$a$$ of length $$n$$.

Your task is to find the maximum possible average value of any subarray$$^{∗}$$ of the array $$a$$.

Formally, for any indices $$l, r$$ such that $$1 $\leq l \leq r \leq n$$$, define the average of the subarray $$a_l, a_{l+1}, \dots, a_r$$ as the sum of elements divided by the number of elements or: $$$\texttt{avg}(l,r) = $\frac{1}{r-l+1} \sum_{i=l}^{r} a_i$$$$ Output the maximum value of $$\texttt{avg}(l,r)$$ over all choices of $$l, r$$.

$$^{∗}$$An array $$b$$ is a subarray of an array $$a$$ if $$b$$ can be obtained from $$a$$ by deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the beginning and several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the end. In particular, an array is a subarray of itself.

The first line contains a single integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each testcase contains a single integer $$n$$ ($$1 $\leq n \leq 10$$$) — the length of the array $$a$$.

The second line of each testcase contains $$n$$ integers $$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$ ($$1 $\leq a_i \leq 10$$$) — the elements of the array.

For each testcase, output a single integer — the maximum average of any subarray of the given array.

It can be shown that the answer is always an integer.
input: Input The first line contains a single integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each testcase contains a single integer $$n$$ ($$1 $\leq n \leq 10$$$) — the length of the array $$a$$. The second line of each testcase contains $$n$$ integers $$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$ ($$1 $\leq a_i \leq 10$$$) — the elements of the array.
output: Output For each testcase, output a single integer — the maximum average of any subarray of the given array. It can be shown that the answer is always an integer.
